jobs.title: Senior GenAI Engineer
jobs.jd: Revolutionize the Future of Logistics as our next Senior Agentic AI Engineer! Are you ready to shape the future of global freight movement with cutting-edge, LLM-driven autonomous agents? We are building the next generation of intelligent automation for the logistics and supply chain industry. We are looking for a Senior GenAI Engineer to design and deploy the workflow and specialized LLM "skills" for our own agent. These solutions will power our platform - spanning the entire lifecycle from freight procurement and rate negotiation to dock scheduling and yard management. About Us: Trimble is an industrial technology company transforming the way the world works by delivering solutions that enable our customers to thrive. We create technologies that connect the digital and physical worlds, helping our customers increase productivity, quality, safety, and sustainability. From purpose-built products to enterprise-level solutions, our technology empowers professionals in construction, geospatial, government, transportation, and more. In the Transportation & Logistics segment, our solutions make it safer, simpler and more efficient to move freight—bringing together a global network of shippers, carriers, brokers and 3PLs. What Makes This Role Great: In this role, you will move beyond basic chatbots and RAG wrappers to architect complex, stateful agentic workflows. You will build systems capable of reasoning through multi-step logistics problems, interacting directly with core systems, and handling the messy, unstructured reality of global supply chains. You thrive on the challenge of turning non-deterministic models into highly reliable, fault-tolerant digital operators that can execute mission-critical logistics tasks. You will work closely with product teams to identify, design, and deliver high-value product and cross-product workflows. The goal is to make a broad set of reusable workflows and native skills available to all our customers and to own their end-to-end adoption, quality, and value. Key Exciting Responsibilities Architect Agentic Workflows: Design and implement robust agentic systems and stateful LLM workflows. You will build skills that can reason through complex scenarios, such as optimizing a freight routing plan, resolving a delayed shipment, or orchestrating trailer moves in a busy yard. Develop Logistics "Skills" & Tooling: Equip our AI agent with the tools they need to take action. Build secure, reliable function-calling interfaces (MCP servers, APIs, webhooks, SQL querying) allowing models to interact seamlessly with external load boards, internal Transportation Management Systems (TMS), and live tracking data. Tame Unstructured Supply Chain Data: Build robust ingestion and extraction pipelines using LLMs and multimodal models to parse complex freight documents, unstructured email negotiations, customs paperwork, and dispatch instructions into structured, actionable data. Design for Reliability & Autonomous Error Recovery: Logistics requires high precision. You will build human-in-the-loop guardrails, deterministic fallbacks, and self-correcting agent loops that ensure the system fails gracefully and escalates to human operators when confidence thresholds are not met. Build Rigorous Eval Pipelines: Move beyond "vibe checks" by creating automated evaluation frameworks to measure agent trajectory success, tool-call accuracy, and reasoning quality across thousands of edge cases in freight, dock, and yard operations. Collaborate with other teams: You will work closely with our product teams to validate which workflows to develop next and how to build them. If our own agent needs improvement or additional capabilities, you’ll make sure to get this resolved as well. Essential Skills & Experience Strong Software Engineering Foundations: 5+ years of experience building and scaling production backend systems. You are fluent in Python (and/or TypeScript/Go) and have deep experience with cloud architecture, microservices, and database design. Deep Applied GenAI & Agent Experience: You have hands-on experience moving beyond simple API calls. You are proficient in function calling/tool use, context window optimization, state management (e.g., LangGraph, AutoGen, or custom state machines), and techniques to reduce hallucination in complex reasoning tasks. Systems Thinking for AI: You understand how to decompose a massive operational problem (like yard orchestration) into smaller, manageable sub-tasks that can be reliably executed by specialized LLM agents and deterministic code. Product & Domain Empathy: You care about the end user's operational reality. You understand that in logistics, an AI agent's mistake can mean a missed delivery window, spoiled freight, or a stalled warehouse. You design with safety and operational efficiency as your top priorities. Pragmatic AI Development: You know when an LLM is the right engine for reasoning, and when traditional optimization algorithms, rules engines, or simple heuristics are the better, faster, and cheaper solution. Bonus Points For: Domain expertise in logistics, supply chain management, freight brokerage, or warehouse operations. Familiarity with standard logistics data formats (EDI, API standards) and platforms (e.g., Project44, Manhattan, Blue Yonder, SAP). Experience with fine-tuning open-weight models (Llama 3, Mistral) for highly specific domain tasks (e.g., JSON extraction from logistics documents, proprietary routing logic). Experience in operations research, constraint programming, or traditional supply chain optimization algorithms. jobs.title: Master Thesis on Robust Agentic HEMS Control using Time-Series Foundation Models via MCP
jobs.jd: Modern Home Energy Management Systems (HEMS) face the challenge of translating complex user requests into concrete, dependable system actions. While state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs) are advancing rapidly in reasoning, multi-modal comprehension, and tool usage, high-precision quantitative modeling of physical signals remains computationally demanding. Specialized Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) offer compelling complementary capabilities for modeling complex numerical curve dynamics, opening up exciting opportunities to explore where and how TSFMs can most effectively support LLM-driven agents. In this Master's thesis, you will research a robust, closed-loop agentic framework where an LLM agent interacts with specialized time-series foundation models via the standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) to analyze, safeguard, and optimize HEMS operations. The thesis can emphasize one or more of the following research directions: Closed-Loop Control & Dynamic Forecasting: Interactive feedback loops for iterative parameter optimization and trajectory simulation. Anomaly Detection & System Guardrails: Real-time identification of abnormal consumption, device faults, and operational constraints. Data Quality & Smart Imputation: Generative zero-shot reconstruction of missing sensor time-series to ensure dependable downstream operation. During your 6-month thesis, your work will focus on the following key areas: During your assignment, you will connect a specialized Time-Series Foundation Model (TSFM) as an independent service to an existing LLM agent ecosystem using the standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP). You will investigate how numerical time-series outputs generated by the TSFM (predictions, reconstructed values, anomaly scores) can be mathematically abstracted at the server level into concise semantic representations tailored for LLM reasoning. Additionally, you will design an interactive evaluation loop where the agent proposes parameter actions, evaluates the model's simulated response or safety feedback, and converges on optimal, robust control decisions. Finally, you will systematically evaluate scenarios and data representations to determine where specialized TSFMs deliver measurable advantages over pure LLM reasoning in terms of computational efficiency, token consumption, latency, and predictive accuracy. Education: master studies in the field of Computer Science, Data Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics or comparable with good grades Experience and Knowledge: strong proficiency in Python (especially familiarity with data and time-series processing libraries such as Pandas and NumPy, as well as modern asynchronous frameworks like asyncio); theoretical and practical grounding in machine learning (ideally time-series models / foundation models); solid understanding of modular software architectures and network interfaces Personality and Working Practice: you are highly self-motivated, using your strong analytical skills to drive independent scientific research Work Routine: we offer you the opportunity to work in a hybrid setup Enthusiasm: strong interest in agentic workflows, tool-calling mechanisms and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Language: very good in English or German Start: according to prior agreement Duration: 6 months Requirement for this thesis is the enrollment at university. Please attach your CV, transcript of records, examination regulations and if indicated a valid work and residence permit. Diversity and inclusion are not just trends for us but are firmly anchored in our corporate culture. Therefore, we welcome all applications, regardless of gender, age, disability, religion, ethnic origin or sexual identity. Need further information about the job? jobs.title: Machine Learning  Engineer
jobs.jd: About the role This is a hands-on senior role. You will write the core code, set the engineering standard for how we build agents, and work directly with clients to turn their workflows into acceptance criteria an agent can be tested against. If you have shipped a LangGraph system to production and can walk us through what broke and how you fixed it, we want to talk to you. What you'll build The runtime Design and build reusable agent runtimes in Python on LangGraph and LangChain, with clean interfaces for models, tools, memory, and integrations. Build stateful workflows with conditional routing, parallel branches, subgraphs, and human approval steps. Add multiple agents only when evaluation results justify the complexity. Reliability Implement durable checkpointing, pause and resume, timeouts, and cancellation. Make retries safe with idempotency keys, deduplication, and reconciliation when the outcome of an external action is unknown. Tools, context, and memory Build tool integrations with validated schemas, scoped permissions, authentication, and structured error handling across enterprise APIs and data systems. Engineer context and memory: retrieval, summarization, context selection, token budgets, retention, and tenant isolation. Evaluation and observability Build evaluation datasets and automated checks for business outcomes, tool-use correctness, policy compliance, and recovery, allowing for valid alternative execution paths. Gate every model, prompt, tool, and graph change on regression results. Instrument agents with LangSmith or equivalent tracing, then use traces to improve task success, latency, and cost per completed workflow. Security Implement prompt-injection defenses, authorization checks, secrets handling, audit trails, and approval controls for sensitive actions. Sandbox code execution where required. Delivery and leadership Own production delivery with backend and platform teams: APIs, streaming, containers, CI/CD, monitoring, incident response, and runbooks. Review code, mentor engineers, and translate client workflows into testable acceptance criteria. What you bring 8+ years of software engineering , including owning production systems from design through operation and hands-on AI/ML application work. 2+ years building LLM applications with LangChain , and at least one LangGraph system you shipped and ran in production. You can explain its architecture, how it failed, how you evaluated it, and what improved. Deep LangGraph knowledge: state schemas, reducers, nodes and edges, conditional routing, subgraphs, checkpointers, interrupts, and persistence. Fluent in current LangChain APIs for tool calling, structured outputs, retrieval, and middleware. Agent harness experience: extending Deep Agents or a comparable harness, including middleware, planning, subagents, filesystem access, and sandboxed execution. Model Context Protocol (MCP): building and securing MCP tool servers, integrated with enterprise identity and access controls. Retrieval engineering: permission-aware RAG, hybrid search, reranking, and retrieval evaluation. Strong Python: async, typing, testing, API design, and maintainable service architecture. Backend and distributed-systems fundamentals: PostgreSQL, queues, concurrency, retries, idempotency, and failure handling. Real experience with LLM failure modes: unreliable tool calls, context limits, nondeterminism, rate limits, and regressions after model or prompt changes. You have used evals and traces to find and fix them. Observability: OpenTelemetry instrumentation alongside LangSmith or equivalent agent tracing. Cloud delivery: Docker, automated testing, and CI/CD on AWS, GCP, or Azure. AI-native development: you work in an AI-enabled software development lifecycle, using coding agents for design, implementation, testing, and review, with the judgment to verify their output and the habits to make a team faster with them. Clear communication: you can explain tradeoffs to engineers and clients and own delivery without close supervision. Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.title: Sr Applied Scientist, Embedded Battery Algorithms, Energy Storage
jobs.jd: Do you want to write the algorithms that control next-generation batteries, and shape the future of energy storage? This role sits where electrochemistry, data/ML, and control theory meet. You will develop the physics-informed and data-driven methods that estimate state of charge, health, power capability, and remaining life, and validate them against lab and fleet data until they are ready to ship. Your algorithms will decide how hard a battery can be pushed, when it needs attention, and how long it will last, so they shape the safety, warranty, and economics of the whole product. You will work side by side with cell, systems, and software engineers, and as an early hire you will help define how we develop and validate battery algorithms. This role can be based in Boston, Irvine, Sunnyvale, or Seattle, and involves occasional domestic and international travel, up to 10% of the time. Key job responsibilities - Develop and own algorithms for state of charge, state of health, power capability, and remaining useful life, combining physics-based models with data-driven and estimation methods. - Deliver validated reference implementations, test vectors, and accuracy targets that define what production code must achieve. - Design the test plans and data needed to develop and validate algorithms, working with the cell and testing teams to turn lab and field data into model improvements. - Analyze algorithm performance across the deployed fleet, find where models drift or fail, and drive improvements. - Own the accuracy and robustness of battery algorithms, and sign off that production implementations match the validated reference. Provide algorithm evidence for safety certification. A day in the life Your week moves between data, models, and experiments. One day you might be working out why a health estimate drifts on cells that have aged in the field, and the next deciding which model structure holds accuracy at cold temperatures. You could be designing a test with the cell team to expose a behavior your model misses, or reviewing an implementation with an applied scientist to confirm that what ships matches what you validated. You will regularly share results with software, systems, and cell leaders, and your findings will shape decisions well beyond the algorithm itself. About the team We are building Amazon's energy storage capability, providing power for advanced technologies while contributing to a stable grid. Our product is highly connected, yet secure and resilient by design. We own it end to end, from software, ML, and controls through system design to cell selection and supply, and on to a safety-certified product in the field. The organization operates like a startup inside Amazon: small, fast-moving, and accountable for our decisions. We work across hardware, software, and science, with suppliers and partners worldwide, and with Amazon infrastructure, procurement, legal, and finance. The organization is at an early stage and growing quickly. You will be among the first algorithm hires, so you will help shape how we design, build, certify, and ship, with a direct line of sight to the product and business decisions your work informs. This is a dynamic role that will regularly present new challenges as the product and organization evolve. - Master's degree in electrical engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, applied mathematics, or a related field. - 8+ years of experience developing battery algorithms or battery models in industry or research with a Master's degree, or 5+ years with a PhD. - Extensive experience launching battery products with leading automotive or grid storage OEMs may be considered in place of some of this experience. - Experience developing state of charge or state of health estimation algorithms for lithium-ion batteries, including building equivalent circuit models and using methods such as Kalman filtering or data-driven models. - Experience validating battery algorithms against laboratory and field data. - Expert proficiency in Python for building and validating battery models, and the ability to prototype algorithms in C. - Familiarity with automotive or battery energy storage system (BESS) safety standards, such as ISO 26262, UL 1973, or UL 9540A. - PhD in electrical engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, applied mathematics, or a related field. - Experience building physics-based electrochemical models, such as the Doyle-Fuller-Newman (DFN) or single particle model (SPM) or other advanced battery models, and with lithium-ion aging mechanisms. - Experience with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, including state of charge estimation across the flat voltage plateau and hysteresis. - Familiarity with lithium-ion failure modes and abuse hazards, such as overcharge, internal short, and thermal runaway, and experience developing algorithms to detect them. - Experience designing battery test protocols, such as hybrid pulse power characterization (HPPC), drive or duty cycles, and impedance spectroscopy. - Experience making technical trade-offs on a safety-critical product, where certification and field reliability constrain cost and schedule. - Comfortable making decisions with incomplete information, and effective across cultures, companies, and time zones. jobs.title: Software Engineer- Agentic AI & Integrations
jobs.jd: ABOUT THE ROLE WIN is seeking highly skilled, hands-on Software Engineers to help build innovative digital applications, AI-powered solutions, and scalable technology platforms. WIN is investing heavily in agentic AI, intelligent automation, and advanced digital platforms to transform how customers access home services and how service professionals deliver them across the $700 billion U.S. home services industry. In this role, you will design and develop software applications, connect internal and external systems, and build intelligent workflows that automate complex business processes. You will work with emerging AI technologies while also contributing to the development of new products and platform capabilities. We are looking for engineers who combine strong software engineering fundamentals with proven experience building real-world AI applications, enjoy solving complex technical challenges, and can turn innovative ideas into reliable, production-ready solutions. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Build software applications and platforms: Design, develop, and maintain scalable backend applications, APIs, and services that power WIN's existing and emerging digital products. Develop agentic AI capabilities: Build and enhance intelligent AI agents and automated workflows that can interact with systems, retrieve information, make decisions within defined parameters, and execute actions to complete business processes. Integrate systems and technologies: Develop robust integrations connecting internal applications, third-party platforms, AI services, and external tools using Python, REST APIs, webhooks, MCP, and other integration technologies. Engineer and optimize AI workflows: Integrate and orchestrate LLMs, AI agents, and external services, including evaluating and switching between AI models and providers to improve accuracy, performance, reliability, and cost efficiency. Ensure reliability and scalability: Build, test, deploy, monitor, and troubleshoot applications and integrations. Implement appropriate safeguards, error handling, and automated testing to ensure secure, dependable performance. Translate business needs into technology solutions: Collaborate with product, technology, and business teams to understand requirements, design technical solutions, and independently deliver working applications and capabilities. Support innovation and product development: Evaluate and implement emerging technologies, contribute to technical architecture, and develop new capabilities that support WIN's expanding digital ecosystem and long-term technology strategy. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 4+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, with strong proficiency in Python and a proven track record of developing backend applications, APIs, and integrations. Demonstrated experience developing and deploying AI/LLM-powered applications, including agentic workflows, tool calling, or AI-driven automation that interacts with external systems. Strong understanding of software architecture, REST APIs, webhooks, authentication, and system integration. Practical experience working with LLM APIs, integrating AI models into applications, and developing workflows that connect AI capabilities with business systems. Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP, databases, SQL, version control, and modern software development and deployment practices. Strong problem-solving and debugging abilities, with demonstrated experience building, testing, and maintaining reliable production applications. Ability to independently own technical deliverables, adapt to emerging technologies, and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol), AI agent frameworks, or similar tool-integration architectures. Experience building conversational AI, voice AI, or real-time automation solutions. Familiarity with FastAPI, asynchronous programming, microservices, or event-driven architectures. Experience with LLM orchestration, RAG, AI evaluation, and performance optimization. Experience developing customer-facing digital products or platforms connecting multiple services, users, or systems. WHY JOIN WIN? Help develop transformative AI-powered capabilities and digital platforms in the $700 billion U.S. home services industry. Work on meaningful, real-world technology initiatives with the opportunity to see your solutions deployed and used. Be part of a high-energy, collaborative team that values innovation, initiative, ownership, and adaptability. Work closely with India-based and US-based teams. Enjoy significant opportunities for learning, professional development, and career growth. Benefit from 100% remote working flexibility and competitive compensation. ABOUT WIN & OUR CULTURE WIN is the #1 ranked inspection services company in the United States. Backed by 35 years of excellence, we are on a mission to build a global brand through cutting-edge technologies, AI-driven innovation, and operational excellence. WIN combines the stability of an established industry leader with the energy and ambition of a technology-driven growth company. We offer talented professionals an opportunity to take ownership, solve meaningful challenges, and contribute to innovations that can reshape our industry.

Experience working with sandbox environments such as Modal, and designing strict access control models to keep user data safe and encrypted at all times. Experience running services in Kubernetes-based environments on GCP or equivalent cloud platforms. Comfort working with Postgres and Redis in high-throughput, low-latency service contexts. jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist
jobs.jd: Porch Group is a leading vertical software and insurance platform and is positioned to be the best partner to help homebuyers move, maintain, and fully protect their homes. We offer differentiated products and services, with homeowners insurance at the center of this relationship. We differentiate and look to win in the massive and growing homeowners insurance opportunity by 1) providing the best services for homebuyers 2) led by advantaged underwriting in insurance 3) to protect the whole home As a leader in the home services software-as-a-service (“SaaS”) space, we’ve built deep relationships with approximately 30 thousand companies that are key to the home-buying transaction, such as home inspectors, mortgage companies, and title companies. In 2020, Porch Group rang the Nasdaq bell and began trading under the ticker symbol PRCH. We are looking to build a truly great company and are JUST GETTING STARTED. Job Title: Senior Data Scientist, Insurance Pricing Location: India Workplace Type: Remote Job Summary The future is bright for the Porch Group , and we'd love for you to be a part of it as our Senior Data Scientist with the Insurance Pricing team . As a Data Scientist on our team, you will build and deploy models that support homeowners insurance pricing and a broader set of business decisions across Porch, including profitability, retention, and customer lifetime value. While GLM-based pricing is an important part of this role, you will apply a wide range of data science techniques — from statistical modeling and machine learning to experimentation, geospatial analysis, and generative AI — to problems across underwriting, pricing, and marketing. You’ll work closely with actuarial, product, and engineering teams to translate Porch’s unique property data into a durable competitive advantage. This is an ideal role for a data scientist who wants to grow their skills across a variety of problems, learn from experienced colleagues, and drive measurable business value. What You Will Do As A Senior Data Scientist, Insurance Pricing Follow and contribute to team modeling standards and best practices, including code quality, documentation, and reproducibility. Learn from and collaborate with senior data scientists, actuaries, and engineers, and share knowledge with the broader team. Build and validate GLM-based models (frequency, severity, and loss cost) that support homeowners insurance pricing. Build machine learning models (GBMs, neural networks, etc.) that drive underwriting accuracy, competitive positioning, and profitability. Develop ensemble models predicting insured-level profitability, customer retention, and conversion, including customer lifetime value (LTV) models to prioritize marketing and underwriting strategies. Incorporate non-traditional data sources — aerial imagery, satellite data, government records, building permits — to quantify localized risk and inform pricing and underwriting decisions. Partner with product, actuarial, engineering, and business stakeholders to scope initiatives and integrate data science solutions into operational workflows. Support the actuarial team in developing, implementing, and monitoring predictive models that meet regulatory requirements. Follow rigorous deployment practices in high-traffic environments, including A/B testing, performance monitoring, and continuous refinement. Apply a broad range of data science methods — statistical modeling, machine learning, experimentation, and causal analysis — to business problems beyond pricing, such as marketing, retention, and operations. Evaluate emerging techniques including generative AI and LLMs to identify new opportunities for competitive advantage. What You Will Bring As A Senior Data Scientist, Insurance Pricing 5+ years of experience in data science, with exposure to insurance pricing, risk modeling, or other applied statistical modeling. Experience owning well-scoped modeling projects from analysis through delivery, and collaborating effectively with cross-functional partners. Experience building and validating statistical and machine learning models, including GLMs, ideally in insurance or another risk-related setting. Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience implementing GLMs and gradient boosting models (scikit-learn, statsmodels, xgboost, lightgbm). Experience with experimental design, including A/B testing models and causal analysis. Familiarity with cloud-based data platforms (e.g., BigQuery, GCP) and MLOps practices such as model training pipelines, versioning, and monitoring. Proficiency with Confluence and Jira for documentation and project tracking in an Agile/Scrum environment. Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field; Master’s or PhD preferred. Nice to have: background in actuarial science or insurance mathematics, including experience collaborating with actuarial teams on regulatory model filing. Nice to have: experience with customer lifetime value, retention, or conversion modeling. Nice to have: experience with geospatial or spatial data analysis (aerial imagery, satellite data, or property-level geographic datasets). Nice to have: exposure to generative AI and LLMs, including prompt engineering or fine-tuning for insurance or financial services use cases. Nice to have: exposure to experimentation frameworks and causal inference methods. Nice to have: experience with model governance, validation frameworks, and regulatory compliance in insurance. Proven experience working with US based business teams. Excellent written and communication skills in English language. Ability to work within core US business hours / time zone expectations - Eastern Standard Time (EST) overlap. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy. We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers. We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade. Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities. jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer
jobs.jd: About Monte Carlo Monte Carlo is the agent trust platform that autonomously observes, fixes, and continuously improves agents and the data that powers them — so enterprises can scale trust at the speed of AI. Bayes, our AI teammate, does the work: detecting, triaging, troubleshooting, and fixing issues in AI agents and the data powering them. The result is self-improving agents that get better with every fix instead of drifting. More than 400 enterprises, including Amazon, PepsiCo, CNN, Nasdaq, and JetBlue, rely on Monte Carlo. Learn more at montecarlo.ai. The Role We're building the products that tell enterprises whether their AI agents can be trusted — and we need someone who works end to end, from an ambiguous problem statement through research, prototyping, and production. You'd get the problem, not the spec: research the approaches, prototype, prove what works, build it, and integrate it into the platform alongside our engineering and data science teams. This role exists because agent observability moved from roadmap to revenue faster than anyone predicted, and the work is now on the critical path. What You'll Do Take an open problem end-to-end — from research and prototyping through production, killing what doesn't work before it becomes someone's roadmap Design and ship agent-powered features — root-cause analysis, incident triage, monitor generation — and integrate them into the platform with our engineering team Build the eval infrastructure that makes those features safe to change: golden datasets, regression suites, offline and online scoring, and the judgment calls about what "good" means Own retrieval and context pipelines over customer metadata, lineage, and query history, and instrument agent behavior in production — traces, failure taxonomies, cost and latency budgets — to close the loop on quality Partner with data science on detection quality and experiment design, and with PM on what an agent should do versus what it merely can do Set the technical bar for how we build with LLMs — patterns, guardrails, and the internal tooling other engineers reuse What We're Looking For You've built agents in production with real users. Not integrated a framework. Not worked on a team that had one. Built them — agents with real autonomy and internal loops, where the model uses tools and decides what to do next without a human in the middle, and you kept them running once real users showed up. RAG with a wrapper doesn't count. Neither does a set of MCP tools point at an API. You've run evals and monitored agents after launch. Agents are non-deterministic, so normal tests don't work on them. You've owned an eval framework — golden datasets, regression suites, offline and online scoring — not a folder of one-off scripts. And you've watched agents in production, not just in dev. Python, plus an ML or data science background. Python is your daily language and you're solid on the backend, though you don't need to be a distributed systems specialist. You understand models well enough to reason about how they behave — you're not an application engineer calling someone else's API. 3+ years in ML, data science, or software engineering — at companies that ship quickly. Startups, AI-native teams, or high-growth product companies where the release cadence is measured in weeks, not quarters. If all of your experience sits inside large, process-heavy organizations with the platform already built for you, this seat will be a hard adjustment. You work from a problem, not a spec. Handed an ambiguous problem statement, you design the experiment, build the smallest version to test it, and take what works into production. You use AI tools every day. Claude or its equivalents are part of how you write code and do research, not something you tried once. This is backend and model layer work, by the way — no frontend. You'd rather ship than polish. Most of this work needs a good answer quickly, not a perfect one eventually. You can tell which problems are the exception and deserve real depth — and you'll say no to the version that demos well and falls apart in production. Nice to have: statistics and hypothesis testing, applied rather than theoretical. Building and maintaining MCP servers. Experience in the data and cloud space — Snowflake, Databricks, dbt, Airflow. This Is Not For You If Your AI work is retrieval with a wrapper, or MCP tools pointed at an API — nothing that decides and acts on its own Your LLM experience is prototypes, notebooks, and demos that never carried production traffic You need a fully specified problem before you start, or you're uncomfortable with the ambiguity of a category being invented in real time Why Monte Carlo We created the data observability category, and we're doing it again with agent trust — you'll build where the market is forming, not where it's settled Series D, $236M raised, backed by Accel, Redpoint, Notable Capital, ICONIQ Growth, and Salesforce Ventures Customers include HubSpot, Fox, Nasdaq, Toast, and Mercado Libre — your work ships to enterprises with real stakes Snowflake Partner of the Year and a verified connector in Anthropic's Claude AI directory Remote-first by design since day one, and recognized as a Best Workplace for it Competitive compensation, equity, and a remote-first environment. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Assistance Foundations
jobs.jd:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

The Assistance Engineering team builds world-class tools for Airbnb's global network of support agents, so guests and hosts get a great experience 24/7, 365 days a year. Airbnb's operational staff must scale with our user base, and we own the entire tech stack behind their success.
Within Assistance Engineering, Assistance Foundations builds the shared platforms that support runs on: case management, the agent workspace, quality and coaching systems, money tooling, data services, agent routing, provisioning and training, and reliability. We are forming a dedicated Machine Learning Engineering group so that intelligence is built once on this foundation and reused across support, rather than rebuilt by each team. You will be one of its founding engineers.

Some of what we are building and shipping:

  • LLM-based quality evaluation that scores support cases against the quality standard, at scale
  • AI coaching that turns quality evidence into coaching plans for team leads
  • Simulation environments that train agents on realistic support scenarios
  • Natural language search and chat tools that help agents and supervisors find answers faster

The Difference You Will Make:

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, you will design, build, and operate the LLM-based and agentic systems behind quality, coaching, case intelligence, and decision support for agents. The work spans prompt design, retrieval, fine-tuning, agent orchestration, dataset engineering, and evaluation. This is a product-building role: you will take systems from first experiment to production and own how they perform for real users.

A Typical Day: 

  • Design, build, and ship LLM-based and agentic systems, from technical design through implementation, experimentation, and deployment.
  • Build offline and online evaluation (human-labeled sets, LLM-as-judge, A/B tests) so that quality is measured, not assumed.
  • Curate and engineer the datasets that prompts, fine-tuned models, and evaluations depend on.
  • Turn one-off models and prompts into shared components that other Foundations teams can adopt.
  • Collaborate with product, design, engineering, data science, and support operations and quality teams to find high-impact problems and quantify results.
  • Participate in design and code reviews, and mentor other engineers.


Your Expertise:

  • 5+ years of industry experience building and shipping applied machine learning, or a PhD in a related field plus 2+ years in industry
  • Recent, hands-on experience building LLM-based systems that shipped to production
  • Expertise in designing and iterating on prompts, fine-tuning, and LLM evaluation
  • Expertise in RAG patterns, memory, tool use, and agent planning
  • Experience integrating LLMs with APIs, vector databases, and orchestration frameworks
  • A solid foundation in machine learning: modeling, evaluation design, experimentation, and A/B testing
  • A track record of shipping AI products used by real users, not only research prototypes or offline models
  • Strong programming (Python, Java, or Kotlin) and the engineering skills to productionize your own work: model serving, monitoring, data pipelines, and safe deployment
  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills to work effectively across teams and domains
  • Bachelor's and/or Master's/PhD degree, preferably in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

 

Your Location:

This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list. If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from.

Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:

Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Threat Research Engineer, Security Factory: Threat Research

jobs.jd:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a senior researcher in GitLab's Threat Research group, you'll turn emerging security threats into protection for GitLab customers. You'll lead your own research projects, taking ideas from the first question to a working proof of concept, deploying it, and analyzing the results. You'll also keep the detection systems you build running in production.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is central to how we work. We build agentic workflows for research, analysis, and detection, and use AI tools every day to move faster. This is a full-stack research role: you'll combine an adversarial mindset with the software engineering skills to build and operate the systems behind your work.

What you’ll do

  • Lead your own research projects, from the first idea to the published result.
  • Research new attack surfaces and threat vectors, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems.
  • Find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in open source projects and developer tools.
  • Analyze supply chain incidents and events.
  • Build AI-powered workflows and agents that automate research, analysis, and detection.
  • Build and maintain the cloud-based systems behind our detection and advisory work.
  • Improve the quality and coverage of our vulnerability and malware advisories.
  • Write up your findings as blog posts and present them at conferences.

What you’ll bring

  • Hands-on security experience in research, malware analysis, penetration testing, or security tooling, with published findings such as Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) records, responsible disclosures, blog posts, or talks.
  • Experience researching AI agents, large language model (LLM) applications, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and using AI in real work through LLM application programming interfaces (APIs) or agent frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or agent software development kits (SDKs).
  • The ability to build systems and assess how to break them, with strong Go or Python skills and practices including testing, code review, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and maintainable code.
  • Experience deploying and running production services on a public cloud.
  • An understanding of package ecosystems and supply chain attacks, informed by current security and AI industry trends.
  • The ability to map attack vectors, explain trade-offs, and use data to move experiments forward while balancing quality, speed, and customer outcomes.
  • Clear writing that explains findings to both engineers and a general audience.
  • Helpful but not required: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experience, infrastructure as code with Terraform or OpenTofu, databases or data pipelines at scale, and reverse engineering.

You don't need deep knowledge of compilers or static application security testing (SAST) engines. A high-level understanding is enough.

You don't have to match every listed requirement exactly to be considered. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply.

About the team

The Threat Research group at GitLab researches security threats as they emerge and turns what we learn into protection for GitLab customers. We maintain the GitLab Advisory Database, which powers GitLab's dependency scanning. We also build detection capabilities, do original vulnerability research, and publish what we find. Recent work includes the Shai-Hulud npm worm and a critical RCE in Serena, a popular MCP coding agent. More on the Security Labs blog.

jobs.jd:
At HelloFresh, the goal is to change the way people eat forever by delivering high-quality food across 18 countries and 3 continents. As a global food solutions group and the world's leading meal kit provider, the portfolio includes HelloFresh, Green Chef, EveryPlate, Chefs Plate, Factor_, and Youfoodz.

Engaging with HelloFresh in Warsaw means collaborating with HelloTech-a global technology division of over 1,000 people powering an end-to-end food ecosystem. From digital personalization, pricing, and forecasting to supply chain optimization and food waste reduction, technology drives every step of this direct-to-consumer model.

About the Role: What's in the Box

HelloTech operates in autonomous, cross-functional alliances, each holding accountability for a specific product domain end to end. In this role, you will join an assigned squad, with the flexibility to transition between teams and projects as technical objectives and business priorities evolve.

Several high-impact machine learning domains are actively hiring, and your project and team placement will be aligned based on your individual strengths, interests, and expertise during the interview process. Key domains include:

  • Risk, Fraud & Payments (Growth Alliance): You will own production ML systems that protect HelloFresh from checkout fraud and intelligently recover failed recurring payments (such as Smart Payment Retry) via low-latency scoring on Databricks.
  • Personalization & Conversions (Growth Alliance): You will build real-time decisioning systems, customer win-back models, and scalable GenAI content pipelines that tailor journeys and messaging across visitor and customer funnels.
  • Dynamic Pricing & Customer Value Optimization (Growth Alliance): You will architect and scale the core Pricing Engine to drive pricing optimization and forecasting across 8 brands, 34 markets, and all weekly menus.

Across all domains, you will work on scalable, high-availability production ML systems serving global architectures. Please note that this is an individual contributor role and does not include people management responsibilities.

What You’ll Do: The Recipe

At HelloFresh, we are moving away from a model where engineers simply execute tickets toward one where product engineers are trusted to own customer problems. As a Product Engineer, you will take a problem, form a point of view, validate it with customers and data, and ship it using AI as a force multiplier.

  • Build and operate data products and machine-learning systems, taking them from experimentation through production and owning their real-world performance.
  • Architect and optimize scalable batch and streaming data pipelines (Python, SQL, PySpark on Databricks, Kafka), feature stores, and low-latency serving infrastructure.
  • Improve inference performance, reliability, and compute cost by profiling bottlenecks, right-sizing infrastructure, and maintaining tight latency targets with dependable fallback mechanisms.
  • Establish and raise modern MLOps standards across teams, including CI/CD automation, model registry versioning, infrastructure as code (Terraform), automated validation gates, and drift detection.
  • Design and execute rigorous experimentation frameworks from A/B tests and holdouts to off-policy evaluation-to credibly measure model impact on core business metrics.
  • Build and scale domain-specific applied AI solutions, ranging from real-time scoring and contextual bandits to production GenAI pipelines with automated quality gates.
  • Collaborate closely with data scientists, software engineers, product managers, and business stakeholders to pressure-test models for production readiness, mentor teammates, and leverage AI coding agents (such as Claude Code or Cursor) to accelerate engineering delivery.

What You’ll Bring: The Ingredients

  • 5+ years building and operating live ML systems in production, paired with the statistical literacy to design sound experiments and interpret their results.
  • Hands-on experience building product-facing ML solutions directly tied to measurable business metrics (such as conversion, retention, revenue, or risk reduction).
  • Deep command of Python, SQL, and large-scale data processing (PySpark on Databricks), paired with solid software engineering practices (testing, clean code, version control) and familiarity with low-latency serving or backend languages like Go.
  • Hands-on background with cloud environments (AWS), containerization, automated CI/CD, and modern ML or orchestration tooling such as Databricks Model Serving, MLflow, SageMaker, Airflow, Kafka, or Terraform.
  • Practical, day-to-day fluency with AI coding tools (like Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot) beyond casual experimentation—knowing how to structure context and set clear boundaries on AI-generated work.
  • A quality-first mindset around model evaluation, drift monitoring, and A/B testing pitfalls for ML systems to ensure bad data or outputs never reach customers.
  • A bias to ship ("finishing the last twenty percent"), strong product sense backed by data, and clear communication skills across international, multi-disciplinary teams.

Nice to have:

  • A track record of optimizing data and ML pipelines for performance and cost at scale.
  • Experience with contextual bandits and off-policy evaluation.
  • Hands-on experience building and running production LLM pipelines.
  • Background in churn prediction and Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) modeling.
  • Prior experience in high-growth consumer tech or subscription-based businesses.

jobs.jd:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Senior Software Engineer, GenAI Platform

 

About the Team

Deliveroo's GenAI Platform team sits within Machine Learning Platform and builds the shared infrastructure that helps DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo teams safely bring GenAI-powered products, agents, automation, and personalisation to production. Our mission is to increase the velocity of business impact from GenAI. A central pillar of that work is running frontier open-weight LLMs and VLMs (such as GLM, Qwen, Kimi, and DeepSeek) ourselves — real-time GPU serving, high-throughput batch inference, and fine-tuning on autoscaling GPUs — delivering large cost and latency wins (for example, a billion embeddings produced roughly 20× cheaper and visual models served roughly 72% cheaper). We also own core platform surfaces including the LLM Gateway, Agent Gateway, evals infrastructure, guardrails, and cost attribution.

 

About the Role

You will join a small, high-leverage team building production infrastructure for Generative AI at Deliveroo and DoorDash, leading the design and architecture of our open-weights model platform spanning inference and fine-tuning: real-time GPU serving, high-throughput batch inference, and model fine-tuning. You’ll set technical direction across model serving and inference engines, fine-tuning and training pipelines, GPU autoscaling and utilization, batch pipelines, backend services, and observability, and mentor engineers as you go. This role is ideal for a senior engineer who enjoys owning ambiguous, high-impact systems and pushing the cost/performance frontier of GPU inference and fine-tuning in a fast-moving technical area where product needs, model capabilities, vendor ecosystems, and cost/performance tradeoffs are evolving quickly.

 

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Lead the design of infrastructure that helps teams move GenAI ideas from prototype to production, increasing the velocity of business impact from AI across the company.

  • Own and evolve our open-weights serving stack — real-time GPU endpoints, high-throughput batch inference, and fine-tuning (SFT/DPO/LoRA) — alongside the LLM Gateway, Agent Gateway, evals infrastructure, guardrails, and cost attribution.

  • Architect scalable, high-performance systems for model serving, batch inference, GPU autoscaling, and fine-tuning that power real customer and internal automation use cases

  • Push the cost and latency frontier of GPU inference — turning batch jobs that took days into hours and cutting inference cost by multiples — while giving product teams a clean choice across open-weight and closed-source models with reliability, fallback, observability, and cost controls built in.

  • Build platforms that support rapid experimentation while meeting production standards for latency, scale, monitoring, SLOs, playbooks, and operational excellence.

  • Partner closely with — and raise the technical bar for — ML engineers, product engineers, data scientists, and platform teams across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo to turn emerging GenAI capabilities into durable platform primitives.

  • Set technical direction for the future of the company's centralised GenAI platform — including emerging directions such as reinforcement learning (RLHF/RLVR), agent optimisation, and other post-training and agentic techniques — enabling the next generation of AI-powered products, agents, automation, and personalisation.

 

We’re excited about you because…

  • BSc, MSc or PhD in Computer Science or equivalent

  • 5+ years of industry experience in software engineering

  • Deep backend engineering fundamentals, especially in Python and distributed systems.

  • Track record of designing and owning production services, APIs, data pipelines, or ML infrastructure at scale.

  • Experience operating systems in production, including observability, debugging, reliability, incident response, and performance/cost optimization.

  • Deep hands-on experience with LLM inference and/or fine-tuning of open-weight models in production — serving (latency, throughput, batching, autoscaling, GPU utilization) and/or fine-tuning (SFT/DPO/LoRA).

  • Demonstrated technical leadership: leading design across ambiguous, fast-moving technical areas, mentoring engineers, and turning customer use cases into reusable platform capabilities

jobs.jd: NVIDIA has helped redefine what computers can do. Now, generative AI is opening new possibilities for how people learn, create, and tackle problems. Your curiosity and scientific judgment can shape what we test, what we learn, and what we build next. You will turn open research questions into rigorous benchmarks, inventive experiments, and tools that reveal how multimodal large language models behave under pressure. Working with researchers and platform engineers, you’ll connect those discoveries to better training methods and safeguards, with reproducible results that inform technical reviews and executive decisions. If you love asking the question no one has thought to test, and building a convincing way to answer it, come help us define what progress in AI safety looks like. Evaluation Methodology: Define metrics and protocols that assess safety alongside model usefulness, using baselines, uncertainty estimates, and failure analysis to distinguish meaningful improvements from noise. Reproducible Evaluation: Build reusable Python pipelines with versioned datasets, model configurations, and experiment tracking to reproduce results and compare performance across model releases. Automated Red-Teaming: Develop tools to discover failure modes and expand evaluation coverage, incorporating human review to validate automated scoring and provide additional judgment. Failure Analysis: Investigate model failures with researchers, document actionable findings, and develop regression tests to assess whether model changes resolve identified issues. Results and Communication: Partner with platform engineers to store and aggregate evaluation results, and clearly communicate findings, limitations, and emerging risks to researchers and decision-makers. What We Need To See: Education and Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, with 6+ years in the field of machine learning engineering or evaluation. Evaluation Design: Experience developing benchmarks, metrics, and statistically sound comparisons for ML systems, including selecting baselines and interpreting uncertainty. Ability to translate ambiguous evaluation questions into testable experiments. Engineering: Strong Python skills and experience building maintainable shared tools, data pipelines, and experiment-tracking workflows. Analytical Rigor: Ability to assess dataset quality, identify limitations in metrics and scoring methods, and support conclusions with reproducible evidence. Communication: Clearly explain findings and tradeoffs to researchers, engineering partners, and executives. Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd: Evaluation: Experience evaluating LLMs, multimodal models, or agentic systems through adversarial testing or automated red-teaming. Community Contributions: Contributions to public benchmarks or evaluation frameworks. Research Publications: A publication track record and interest in continuing to publish at top tier venues. Human-Aligned Evaluation: Experience validating model-based evaluators against human judgments or designing human-in-the-loop evaluation workflows. Statistical Rigor: Strong model evaluation skills and a commitment to sound statistical practices, including confidence intervals. jobs.jd: If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/ About Us Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day. We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process. About the Role We're looking for a data scientist with strong statistics and modeling skills to be the science partner for the machine learning and recommendation systems behind Twitch's discovery products. You will work with product managers, ML engineers and applied scientists to help build what our recommendation systems should optimize for. That means balancing what a viewer does today (a click, a play, minutes watched) against what keeps them coming back: return visits, daily habits, and lasting connections with creators. It also means weighing short-form clips against long-form live content, and each surface against the others. This role will draw from a variety of statistical learning techniques, causal inference, optimization and recommender systems evaluation, and it still owns the full path from question to decision. Reporting to the Director of Data Science, you will work from our San Francisco, CA office. You Will - Help define the objective functions and success metrics for ranking and recommendations across feeds, search and notifications. Make the trade-offs explicit between short-term engagement (clicks, plays, watch time) and long-term outcomes (return visits, retention, new creator connections), including how short-form clips and live content add to or take away from each other. - Evaluate ranking, recommendation and feed changes with ML engineers and applied scientists. This covers A/B tests and long-running holdouts, offline metrics that predict online results, and the cost and value of exploration and cold start. Handle the hard cases: novelty effects, interference between experiments, two-sided marketplace effects involving creators and viewers, and feedback loops in recommendation data. - Build statistical and ML models that explain viewer behavior and size opportunities, such as propensity, uplift, survival and retention models. Include proxy metrics that predict long-term retention, so teams can decide in days rather than months. - Turn ambiguous product questions into clear analyses. Quantify the uncertainty, and make recommendations that inform the machine learning and discovery roadmap. - Define the logging and data needed to measure discovery surfaces, and check its quality. - Contribute to the team's standards for experimentation, causal inference and model evaluation, and share what you learn with other data scientists. Perks - Medical, Dental, Vision & Disability Insurance - 401(k) - Maternity & Parental Leave - Flexible PTO - Amazon Employee Discount About the team Twitch is all about community, and our Community team is a core pillar of what makes Twitch, Twitch. Community Discovery & ML (CDML) helps millions of viewers find the creators and communities they'll love. That covers search, browse, the mobile live and clips feeds, recommended notifications, and the recommendation systems behind them. When a viewer finds a new creator through one of these, it's often the start of a lasting connection. That connection is what keeps viewers, and the creators they watch, coming back. - 3+ years of data scientist experience - A BA/BS in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science or a related quantitative field, or equivalent industry experience. - 3+ years as a data scientist in a high-velocity, data-driven environment, with hands-on experience applying statistical modeling and machine learning (regression, classification, causal inference, time series), including the assumptions behind each method and when it fails. - Experience designing and analyzing online experiments, including variance reduction, power analysis and the pitfalls of interpreting results. - Expert SQL and proficiency in Python or R. - A track record of using data and models to influence product decisions and leadership. - An MS or PhD in a quantitative field. - Experience with recommender systems, search ranking or feed ranking, such as offline evaluation (precision and recall, NDCG), exploration versus exploitation, or cold-start problems. - Experience with multi-objective optimization or with defining objective functions for ranking systems, including choosing weights between competing goals. - Experience building proxy metrics for long-term outcomes, or estimating long-term effects from long-running holdouts or observational data (e.g., difference-in-differences, synthetic control, uplift modeling). - Experience with two-sided platforms or marketplaces, where changes for viewers also affect creators or supply. - Experience on a consumer content platform: streaming, short-form video, social or marketplaces. - Familiarity with Twitch, as a viewer or a creator (or both!). jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer - Recommendations
jobs.jd:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Global Engineering teams tackle complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace, building and scaling systems that serve millions of customers, riders and partners every day.

We're looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our London office as part of a Global DoorDash Engineering team (working hybrid, 3 days in the office).

This role sits in our Consumer Org, where you'll work on recommendation problems with direct, measurable impact on how customers discover relevant content. You’ll collaborate with experienced scientists and engineers across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt, learning from multiple recommendation systems while helping shape the next generation of the experience.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design, develop and improve recommendation, ranking and retrieval models that surface relevant restaurants, dishes, items and content to customers.
  • Own applied ML problems end to end: frame the problem, analyze data, develop models, define offline evaluation, run experiments and monitor production performance.
  • Develop methods that balance relevance with product and customer needs, such as diversity, availability, business constraints and changing user intent.
  • Collaborate closely with Software Engineers, ML Engineers, Product Managers and Analysts to turn scientific insights into reliable customer-facing products.
  • Evaluate and apply state-of-the-art ML methods where they meaningfully improve recommendation quality, robustness or efficiency.
  • Contribute to a high bar for applied-science practice through technical reviews, knowledge sharing and thoughtful experimentation.

What You'll Need to Thrive

  • You have substantial hands-on experience applying machine learning to real-world problems and a track record of bringing models from development into production; a PhD with relevant applied research experience is equally welcome.
  • You have experience with recommendation systems, ranking, retrieval, personalisation, or closely related ML problems.
  • You can independently turn an ambiguous customer or product problem into a well-scoped ML approach, make sound trade-offs and drive it to a measurable outcome.
  • You are proficient in Python and experienced with modern ML frameworks and large-scale data processing.
  • You understand how to evaluate ML systems rigorously, including offline metrics, experiment design and interpreting online results.
  • You communicate complex technical ideas clearly and work effectively with cross-functional partners.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale
Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.

🌱 See your impact, fast
Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment.

🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership
Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.

🌎 A culture built for builders
High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation
jobs.location: US, CA, Santa Clara US, TX, Remote US, PA, Remote US, WA, Remote US, CA, Remote US, MA, Remote
jobs.jd: Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what's never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world's best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you'll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world. We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our new User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation team. You will own the systems our research runs on: the architecture, scale, and releases of our open-source framework. You'll also build the environments where simulated users meet models and agents. User simulation is quickly becoming core infrastructure for evaluating and training AI models and agents. They are judged by how they work with users, people or other agents, over many turns: holding a conversation, using tools, or collaborating on code in a real repository. Real data is thinnest here: slow and costly to collect, skewed toward existing users, and missing the long tail of languages, domains, and safety scenarios. We build grounded synthetic users and simulators, then use both to find capability gaps and close them with targeted training data and RL environments. A lot of our work ships as open source, including NeMo User Sim, Nemotron-Personas, and the data and environments we generate. We build our own systems on these same tools. We publish and present at top conferences, and we organize UserSim @ NeurIPS 2026, the first NeurIPS workshop on user simulation. The team serves three groups: Internal partners , including Nemotron and other model, agent, and product teams who evaluate and train their models with our simulators. Open-source users and contributors who build on the framework for their own models, agents, and languages. The research community , through work that pushes the state of the art and is published at top venues. The mission is the boss. We organize around the problem, not titles or ownership. Researchers write production code, engineers shape research, and everyone works directly with partner teams. We share credit, review each other's work candidly, and pick up whatever moves the mission forward. What you'll be doing: Own the architecture of NeMo User Sim: the conversation engine, configuration-driven pipelines, and extension API. Scale simulation to tens of thousands of concurrent multi-turn episodes against hosted and self-served models (e.g., vLLM, NIM), sharded across Slurm or Kubernetes. Runs must survive rate limits and partial failures, resume cleanly, and reproduce down to the row. Build and run environments for agents. These include stateful simulated tool services, and sandboxed coding environments where simulated users work with coding agents on real repositories. Verifiers and hidden tests grade the results. Connect simulated users to NeMo Gym and RL training, and keep the loop fast and cheap. Turn research prototypes into reliable, tested features together with research scientists. Run the open-source project: versioned releases, CI/CD, dependency and license hygiene, issue triage, and contributor reviews. Build the pipelines behind our open data releases, onboard internal partner teams, and present the framework at conferences. What we need to see: BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience). 6+ years building production ML systems, data pipelines, or developer libraries. Expert Python skills, with a track record of typed, tested libraries that other teams depend on. Experience running LLM workloads at scale: serving (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, NIM), concurrency, and cost. Experience with LLM evaluation, training-data pipelines, or agents that use tools. Strong software design judgment on interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility, with the mission ahead of ownership and credit. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Maintaining a widely used open-source ML library. RL training infrastructure or environments, such as NeMo Gym or NeMo RL. Infrastructure for coding agents: container sandboxes and SWE-bench-style harnesses. Inference optimization: distillation, quantization, or speculative decoding. Experience with NeMo Data Designer, Ray, or Spark and experience with multilingual text processing, such as language identification, scripts, and localization. jobs.jd:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Global Engineering teams tackle complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace, building and scaling systems that serve millions of customers, riders and partners every day.

We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join our London office as part of a Global DoorDash Engineering team (working hybrid, 3 days in the office).

Our New Verticals team exists to grow monthly active usage outside of restaurant ordering — groceries, retail, and everything in between. That means turning someone who only orders restaurant food into someone who also uses the app for a grocery run, and turning dormant users into active ones. You'll work on the surfaces that make that happen: the homepage, vertical landing pages, and the notifications that bring people back. This role sits closer to the personalisation and ranking side of that mission, working alongside colleagues across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Build and improve ranking models for vertical landing pages (grocery, retail), deciding what a user sees first when they land on a store page
  • Design models that blend new-vertical content into a homepage built around restaurant ordering, without disrupting the core experience
  • Build personalisation models that translate a user's existing behaviour into relevant recommendations for verticals they haven't tried yet
  • Contribute to notification targeting — who gets notified, with what message, and when, to drive adoption of new verticals

What You'll Need to Thrive

  • Minimum 3+ years of experience as an ML Engineer or Data Scientist, with a proven ability to write high-quality production code in Python
